parameters.name: Heart rate (resting)
parameters.space_reference: Resting rate unchanged after 3–6 months. Exercise sessions average 131–135. Fit crew may rest below 50
parameters.advisory: 41–50 or 91–110 at rest (NEWS2 score 1) unless inside own band; drift ≥3 spreads from own median
parameters.caution: ≤40 or ≥131 at rest (single NEWS2 score of 3)
parameters.warning: Part of a NEWS2 total of 5–6; irregular pulse with symptoms
parameters.emergency: NEWS2 total ≥7; with chest pain, fainting or collapse
parameters.actions: 1) Confirm after 5 min at rest (persistence rule). 2) Check activity tag: no high-rate score during logged exercise or spacewalk. 3) If irregular, very fast or very slow at rest: stop exertion, record a 12-lead ECG. 4) Ask about chest pain, breathlessness, fainting. 5) Re-check per tier.
parameters.recipients: Crew medical officer reviews ECG; ECG sent to ground / flight surgeon
parameters.source: MedlinePlus; Norsk 2015; NEWS2 (RCP); NASA cardiovascular risk

parameters.name: Blood pressure – systolic
parameters.space_reference: 24-h systolic ≈8 mmHg lower in long flight; night-time dip kept
parameters.advisory: 101–110 only if below own in-flight band (score 1); drift from own baseline
parameters.warning: ≤90 with light-headedness or fainting; NEWS2 total 5–6
parameters.actions: 1) Lie flat or secure in place. 2) Oral fluids. 3) Check fluid intake and urine output, any bleeding, recent medicines, heart rhythm. 4) Re-check in 1 h. 5) Before landing or a gravity change: fluid loading and compression garments per checklist.
parameters.basis: Clinical band (NEWS2) + Norsk 2015 shift; adjustment ours
parameters.source: Norsk 2015; NEWS2; NASA orthostatic intolerance brief

parameters.name: Blood pressure – diastolic
parameters.space_reference: 24-h diastolic ≈9 mmHg lower
parameters.actions: Re-measure after 5 min rest; interpret with systolic and symptoms; follow the systolic protocol if both are low.
parameters.recipients: Crew member; CMO if systolic also flags

parameters.name: Breathing rate
parameters.space_reference: No in-flight range published: Earth range + own baseline
parameters.actions: 1) Read cabin CO2 and O2 where the person is (cabin first). 2) Re-measure at rest. 3) Check SpO2 and end-tidal CO2. 4) Chest exam; recent spacewalk; neck or leg swelling (clot). 5) Oxygen by mask if SpO2 low.
parameters.recipients: CMO; emergency tier: whole crew and ground at once

parameters.name: Oxygen saturation (SpO2)
parameters.space_reference: No shift in a sea-level cabin; lower in a reduced-pressure exploration cabin (reset baseline after any atmosphere change)
parameters.actions: 1) Re-check sensor and perfusion index (reject poor signal). 2) Read cabin O2 and pressure. 3) Oxygen by mask if ≤93% at rest (supplemental O2 adds 2 NEWS2 points). 4) Breathing rate, chest exam, recent spacewalk, neck or leg swelling.
parameters.recipients: CMO; ground if caution or above
parameters.source: StatPearls; NEWS2; NASA habitable atmosphere brief

parameters.name: Body temperature (core)
parameters.space_reference: Resting value rises ≈1 °C by 2.5 months, plateau near day 75. Exercise peaks ≈1.4 °C higher, some crew >40 °C
parameters.actions: 1) Rest, fluids, re-check in 1 h. 2) Look for a source: urine, skin, chest, teeth. 3) White-cell count if analyser available. 4) Check recent exercise or spacewalk thermal load. 5) Log symptoms.
parameters.recipients: Flight surgeon decides on antibiotics (limited stock and shelf life)
parameters.basis: Clinical band (NEWS2) + Stahn 2017 shift; adjustment ours
parameters.source: Stahn 2017; NEWS2; NASA urinary health brief

parameters.name: Consciousness / alertness
parameters.unit: Alert / new confusion / voice / pain / unresponsive
parameters.space_reference: Same
parameters.emergency: Any new confusion, response only to voice or pain, or unresponsive (NEWS2 score 3)
parameters.actions: Emergency checklist: secure the person, airway–breathing–circulation, continuous monitoring, check cabin O2/CO2/pressure at that spot, recent spacewalk (decompression sickness), blood glucose, head injury. First aid does not wait for Earth.
parameters.recipients: Whole crew and ground at once

parameters.name: Acute early-warning score (NEWS2 total)
parameters.space_reference: Space adjustments for BP, temperature and pulse (ours)
parameters.actions: Follow the tier response: Advisory self-care prompt; Caution CMO review within the hour; Warning exam now and treatment from the medical checklist; Emergency checklist immediately.

parameters.name: Heart-rate variability
parameters.space_reference: No in-flight reference
parameters.actions: Check sleep, stress, workload and signs of illness; no stand-alone alert.

parameters.name: ECG rhythm, ST and QT flags
parameters.space_reference: Arrhythmia is a named NASA cardiovascular risk
parameters.emergency: Flag with chest pain, fainting or collapse
parameters.actions: 1) Stop exertion. 2) Record 12-lead ECG. 3) Ask about chest pain, breathlessness, fainting. 4) Check electrolytes if analyser available. 5) Send ECG to ground.
parameters.recipients: CMO; ECG to ground / flight surgeon
parameters.source: Tempus Pro spec 44-2001EN-02; NASA cardiovascular risk

parameters.name: End-tidal CO2
parameters.space_reference: No in-flight range
parameters.caution: Outside 35–45 while cabin CO2 is normal (ours)
parameters.actions: Compare with cabin CO2: if cabin CO2 is high, treat the cabin first. Otherwise check breathing rate, SpO2, chest exam.

parameters.name: Carboxyhaemoglobin (SpCO)
parameters.cadence: After smoke, fire or chemical event
parameters.caution: Any rise from baseline after a cabin event (ours)
parameters.warning: Rise + cabin event in last 24 h (smoke/toxic pattern)
parameters.actions: Leave the affected module, oxygen/mask per cabin fire/toxic checklist, read combustion-product monitors (CO, HCN, HCl, HF).

parameters.name: Methaemoglobin (SpMet)
parameters.caution: Any rise from baseline after a cabin event (ours)
parameters.warning: Rise + cabin event in last 24 h
parameters.actions: Same as SpCO: leave the area, follow the toxic-release checklist, check cabin monitors.

parameters.name: Perfusion index
parameters.actions: Signal-quality gate only: if low, reject the SpO2 reading, warm and reposition the sensor, re-measure.

parameters.name: Haemoglobin, non-invasive (SpHb)
parameters.space_reference: Rises early in flight, then returns to pre-flight
parameters.advisory: Sustained shift ≥2 g/dL from own baseline (2× sensor error, ours)
parameters.caution: Below Earth range in flight (unexpected; ours)
parameters.actions: Confirm with lab haemoglobin if available; look for bleeding or haemolysis; note hydration.

parameters.name: Haemoglobin (lab)
parameters.cadence: ~Flight day 30 and 30 days before return; on symptoms
parameters.space_reference: Mean 14.1 → 15.0 early, then back to pre-flight; falls to ≈13.5 on landing day (expected)
parameters.actions: Look for bleeding or severe haemolysis; repeat count; a dip after landing is expected.

parameters.name: Haematocrit
parameters.space_reference: ≈10–12% above pre-flight through the mission (plasma volume reduced)
parameters.actions: Read with hydration status; check fluid intake.

parameters.name: Platelets
parameters.space_reference: Raised early and mid-flight
parameters.caution: Outside range with clot risk factors or neck-vein flow change (ours)
parameters.actions: Read with clot risk factors and jugular ultrasound findings.

parameters.name: White cells and lymphocytes
parameters.cadence: On symptoms; after a radiation event
parameters.space_reference: Use Earth range
parameters.caution: Outside range with fever or infection signs (ours)
parameters.warning: Falling lymphocyte count after a suspected large radiation dose
parameters.actions: After a suspected large dose: repeat counts every 2–3 h for 8–12 h (falling lymphocytes estimate dose). With fever: source hunt (urine, skin, chest, teeth).

parameters.name: Serum calcium
parameters.space_reference: Stays regulated despite bone loss
parameters.caution: Out of range (abnormal in space as on Earth; tier ours)
parameters.actions: Repeat test; check ECG; review supplements and medicines.

parameters.name: 25-OH vitamin D
parameters.space_reference: Falls in flight even with supplements
parameters.caution: <20: treat and recheck in 3 months (per flight surgeon)
parameters.actions: Review supplement adherence and diet; flight surgeon sets any change.

parameters.name: Ferritin / serum iron
parameters.space_reference: Ferritin higher after ISS flights; serum iron raised in flight
parameters.actions: Interpret as altered iron handling from red-cell breakdown; review diet iron.

parameters.name: Creatinine
parameters.cadence: When a kidney stone is suspected
parameters.space_reference: Use Earth range
parameters.actions: Check with white count, urinalysis and kidney ultrasound when stone suspected; push fluids.

parameters.name: Sodium (serum)
parameters.space_reference: No in-flight range found
parameters.caution: Outside range with symptoms (confusion, cramps, weakness; ours)
parameters.actions: Repeat; review fluid and sodium intake; check medicines.

parameters.name: Potassium (serum)
parameters.space_reference: No in-flight range found
parameters.actions: Repeat; record ECG; review medicines and diet.

parameters.name: Blood sugar (glucose)
parameters.device: Continuous glucose sensor; finger-stick; manual entry
parameters.space_reference: No in-flight range published; sensor first worn on ISS in 2025
parameters.advisory: Fasting reading outside range, or drift from own baseline (ours)
parameters.caution: Outside range with symptoms: sweating, shaking, confusion (ours)
parameters.actions: 1) Tag fasting or after meal; re-measure. 2) If low with symptoms: fast-acting carbohydrate per medical checklist, re-check in 15 min. 3) Review food intake and timing.

parameters.name: Cortisol : DHEA ratio (saliva)
parameters.space_reference: Rises in flight
parameters.advisory: Sustained rise vs baseline when results return
parameters.actions: Log sample; review sleep, stress and workload; watch for virus reactivation symptoms.

parameters.name: Herpes virus DNA (saliva/urine)
parameters.space_reference: Shed by 96% (EBV), 65% (VZV), 61% (CMV) of ISS crew tested
parameters.caution: Detected with rash, cold sores or shingles-type pain
parameters.actions: Usually silent: act on symptoms (see infection signs).

parameters.name: Urine specific gravity and pH
parameters.space_reference: Use Earth range
parameters.actions: Increase fluid intake; re-test next day.

parameters.name: Urinary calcium
parameters.space_reference: Higher in flight; whole-body calcium loss 200–300 mg/day
parameters.advisory: Rising or above range: check exercise loads and fluid intake
parameters.actions: Check resistive-exercise loads and fluid intake; vitamin D status; sodium intake.
parameters.recipients: Flight surgeon (potassium citrate carried on ISS at their discretion)
parameters.source: Smith, NASA; NBME; NASA bone loss brief

parameters.name: Bone resorption markers (NTX)
parameters.space_reference: Resorption rose from 427 to 668 mg calcium/day in flight
parameters.actions: Review resistive-exercise loads; vitamin D; fluid; flight surgeon review.

parameters.name: Urine volume
parameters.space_reference: Flight lowers volume and raises calcium; output >2.5 L/day kept stone risk lowest
parameters.actions: Hydration mission in the daily flight plan; re-check next day.

parameters.name: Urine colour
parameters.space_reference: Concentrated urine raises stone risk
parameters.actions: Drink more; log fluid intake; re-check.

parameters.name: Flank pain or blood in urine
parameters.space_reference: Stone risk raised in flight
parameters.caution: Any flank pain or blood in urine
parameters.warning: With fever or inability to pass urine (ours)
parameters.actions: 1) Fluids. 2) Pain relief from the medical checklist. 3) Kidney ultrasound (guided), urinalysis, white count, creatinine. 4) Ground consult.
parameters.recipients: Ground consult (stones rank 2nd among likely ISS evacuation causes in NASA's model)

parameters.name: Cannot pass urine / painful urination
parameters.space_reference: Retention more common in women in flight
parameters.actions: Act the same shift: bladder ultrasound; catheterisation per checklist is the main treatment; with fever, source hunt.

parameters.name: Fluid intake
parameters.space_reference: ≥2.5 L/person/day provided, +240 mL per spacewalk hour
parameters.actions: Hydration task; carry a drink bag; log intake.

parameters.name: Bone density (DXA)
parameters.device: DXA scan before and after flight only
parameters.space_reference: Loss ≈1–1.5% per month
parameters.lower_limit: Hip & spine <95% of pre-mission; femoral neck <90% (V1 4027)
parameters.actions: In flight track proxies: resistive exercise done, calcium and vitamin D intake, urinary calcium. App shows 'not measurable in flight'.
parameters.source: NASA-STD-3001 Vol 1 V1 4027; bone loss brief

parameters.name: Resistance exercise done vs planned
parameters.space_reference: Main in-flight countermeasure for bone and muscle
parameters.caution: Exercise below plan 7 days + fitness <80% (deconditioning pattern)
parameters.actions: Review exercise log; check for injury, device fault or schedule pressure; rebuild plan.

parameters.name: Exercise minutes
parameters.space_reference: ≈600 min/week prescribed on ISS
parameters.actions: Add exercise task to the flight plan; review barriers.

parameters.name: Aerobic capacity (VO2max)
parameters.device: Periodic fitness test; exercise heart-rate response
parameters.space_reference: Average fall 7.4% on ISS; 12–21% of crew fell >20% at some point
parameters.caution: <80% of pre-mission; below EVA floor before a spacewalk
parameters.actions: Review exercise log; check injury, device, schedule; no spacewalk without medical clearance (V1 6006).
parameters.recipients: Exercise specialists; flight surgeon clears EVA

parameters.name: Muscle strength
parameters.space_reference: Falls without loading (70-day bed rest without exercise: −23% knee extension)
parameters.actions: Increase resistive loading per specialist; check injury.

parameters.name: Body mass
parameters.space_reference: Crews tend to under-eat
parameters.actions: Review food log; add preferred, energy-dense items; check nausea, mood, taste changes; nutrition review.

parameters.name: Food energy intake
parameters.space_reference: ISS intake averaged ≈2,300–2,450 kcal/day; V1 4020 asks for 100% of requirement
parameters.actions: Review food log; preferred and energy-dense foods; check nausea, mood, taste; vitamin D check.

parameters.name: New blur or blind spot (SANS symptom)
parameters.space_reference: ≈70% of crew show ≥1 SANS sign; ≈18% clinically concerning
parameters.caution: Any new blur, blind spot or eye-test change (after day 30)
parameters.actions: Same day: near and far acuity and Amsler grid; book OCT, fundoscopy, tonometry, eye ultrasound; review cabin CO2 history.
parameters.recipients: Flight surgeon and eye specialist; switch to stronger on-board lenses

parameters.name: Retinal thickness around optic disc (OCT)
parameters.space_reference: Earliest SANS sign
parameters.caution: Change ≥55 µm or optic-disc swelling Frisén grade ≥1
parameters.actions: Repeat imaging; acuity and Amsler grid; review CO2 history.

parameters.name: Visual acuity and Amsler grid
parameters.caution: Any new distortion or loss of acuity
parameters.actions: Repeat test; follow the vision-change protocol.

parameters.name: Neck-vein (internal jugular) flow
parameters.cadence: ≈Day 30, day 60, 6 weeks before return; on symptoms
parameters.space_reference: 6 of 11 crew had stagnant or reversed flow near day 50; one occlusive clot
parameters.caution: Stagnant or reversed flow; new facial/eyelid swelling with headache
parameters.actions: Hydrate; bring the next scan forward; check family history, clotting disorder, hormone use. With a clot: no spacewalks or heavy resistive exercise for ≥30 days.

parameters.name: Standing tolerance (BP/HR on standing)
parameters.device: Monitor after landing or on a surface
parameters.space_reference: Plasma volume falls ≈15% in first 2 days; problem appears on return to gravity
parameters.actions: Sit or lie down; fluids; compression garments; before landing: fluid loading per checklist.

parameters.name: Motion sickness
parameters.cadence: Daily in week 1 and after each gravity change
parameters.space_reference: ≈73–79% affected in first days; mild clears in 36–48 h, moderate in 72 h
parameters.caution: Grade 3 (>2 vomiting episodes, marked lethargy) or symptoms past 72 h (tier ours)
parameters.actions: Limit head movement; anti-nausea medicine from the checklist (promethazine is NASA's first choice; dose per checklist); hydration; regrade daily. No spacewalk until clear, none within 72 h of launch; IV fluids if severe.

parameters.name: Balance / dizziness
parameters.cadence: Daily for 1 week after each transition
parameters.space_reference: Altered after gravity changes
parameters.actions: Limit fast head movements; avoid hazardous tasks; re-check daily.

parameters.name: Hearing thresholds
parameters.space_reference: Constant fan/pump noise
parameters.actions: Check personal noise dose; wear hearing protection; re-test; check ear block.

parameters.name: Headache
parameters.space_reference: 54% reported headaches in an ISS medication study
parameters.advisory: Any headache → check cabin CO2 (cabin-first pattern)
parameters.emergency: Sudden severe headache with neurological signs
parameters.actions: Read CO2 where the person has been working; move to moving air; restore airflow; check if other crew have the same symptom.
parameters.recipients: CMO if persists or vision changes
parameters.source: NASA CO2 brief; ISS medication study

parameters.name: Infection signs (rash, cold sores, shingles pain, fever)
parameters.space_reference: 61% of ISS crew shed a reactivated herpes virus; stress hormones rise
parameters.caution: Rash, cold sores, shingles-type pain, lasting fever, or an infection that does not clear (tier ours)
parameters.actions: Photo log; temperature; white count if available; isolate items; follow medical checklist.

parameters.name: Skin: rash, dryness, cut, abrasion
parameters.cadence: On symptoms; daily photo until healed
parameters.space_reference: Most frequent in-flight complaint (~10 abrasions and 10 rashes per mission in NASA model)
parameters.caution: Signs of infection: spreading redness, pus, fever (ours)
parameters.actions: Clean and dress per checklist; daily photo; moisturiser for dryness.

parameters.name: Aches and injuries
parameters.space_reference: Back pain, exercise and suit injuries common
parameters.warning: After spacewalk with tingling or skin change (decompression check)
parameters.actions: Rest the area; review exercise technique; pain relief from checklist; ultrasound if guided scan available.

parameters.name: Medication taken and stock
parameters.space_reference: 71% used sleep medication in an ISS study
parameters.advisory: Stock of an item below planned need (ours)
parameters.actions: Log effect and side effects; report low stock to ground. The app never suggests a drug or dose.

parameters.name: Sleep duration
parameters.space_reference: ≈6–6.5 h on Shuttle and ISS
parameters.advisory: <6 h three nights running, 7-day average <6 h, or awake >16 h
parameters.caution: Short sleep + slower reaction test (fatigue pattern)
parameters.actions: Protect the next sleep period; no caffeine 6–12 h before sleep; bright light after waking, dim light 1–2 h before bed; check noise, light, temperature and CO2 in the sleep station; lighter task list.
parameters.recipients: Schedule change through ground; sleep medicines only via flight surgeon

parameters.name: Sleep timing / circadian alignment
parameters.space_reference: ISS crews see 16 sunrises a day; shifts follow docking and EVA schedules
parameters.advisory: Sleep midpoint drifting from schedule; critical tasks planned in body-clock low (≈1–7 AM)
parameters.actions: Light schedule (bright after waking, dim before bed); move critical tasks out of the low.

parameters.name: Mood
parameters.space_reference: Stress, low mood, anxiety and conflict are the common problems
parameters.advisory: 3 days at ≥2 points below own median (ours)
parameters.caution: Sustained drop with withdrawal, loss of appetite or interest (tier ours)
parameters.actions: Private check-in; repeat cognitive test; rule out CO2, low O2, sleep loss and medicine effects first.
parameters.recipients: Private psychological conference; adjust workload and family contact

parameters.name: Stress
parameters.space_reference: Same contributors as mood
parameters.advisory: 3 days at ≥2 points above own median (ours)
parameters.caution: Sustained with sleep or mood change (ours)
parameters.actions: Same as mood; review workload.

parameters.name: Workload (Bedford) / effort (Borg CR10)
parameters.space_reference: Same limits
parameters.advisory: Ratings above limits on repeated days
parameters.actions: Rebalance task list; flag to ground planners.

parameters.name: Reaction time (3-min PVT-B)
parameters.space_reference: Slows with sleep loss
parameters.advisory: Slower than own baseline two tests running (ours)
parameters.actions: Check sleep; lighter task list and wind-down task; re-test.

parameters.name: Cognition battery (10 tests)
parameters.space_reference: Monthly WinSCAT on ISS
parameters.actions: Retest after head injury, illness, or a CO2 or low-oxygen event; rule out environment and sleep.
parameters.source: UPenn Cognition; NASA behavioural health brief

parameters.name: Team cohesion / conflict
parameters.space_reference: Isolation and confinement strain teams
parameters.actions: Private conference; crew-support activities; workload review.

parameters.name: Heart rate during spacewalk
parameters.space_reference: Seen in NASA surface-EVA simulations
parameters.actions: Slow pace; rest; hydrate.

parameters.name: Core temperature during spacewalk
parameters.actions: Slow pace; increase suit cooling; rest.

parameters.name: Suit pressure, O2, CO2, metabolic rate
parameters.space_reference: Per suit flight rules
parameters.caution: Suit value outside suit flight rule (ours)
parameters.actions: Follow suit-malfunction procedure; end spacewalk and return to airlock.

parameters.name: Decompression sickness symptoms
parameters.space_reference: Risk follows spacewalks and cabin pressure changes
parameters.warning: Type I: joint pain or itching within 24 h
parameters.emergency: Type II: numbness, weakness, confusion or breathing trouble
parameters.actions: 1) Stop activity. 2) 100% oxygen. 3) Neurological check. 4) Repressurise suit and cabin per protocol (no hyperbaric chamber in flight).

parameters.name: Dust exposure symptoms (eyes, throat, cough)
parameters.space_reference: Apollo crews reported eye, skin and airway irritation
parameters.advisory: Eye, throat or cough symptoms within 24 h of suit removal (ours)
parameters.actions: Rinse eyes; clean suit and airlock; check cabin dust reading; mask if needed.
parameters.basis: NASA lunar dust brief; tier ours

parameters.name: Cumulative effective dose (personal)
parameters.space_reference: ISS ≈40–90 mSv per 6 months; Mars round trip ≈1,000 mSv
parameters.actions: Track from day one; plan EVA and shielding to reduce dose; take dose from dosimeters, never a lookup.
parameters.recipients: Flight surgeon; radiation team on ground

parameters.name: Daily dose rate (cabin and personal)
parameters.space_reference: ISS ≈0.2–0.5; Mars transit 1.8; Mars surface 0.67
parameters.upper_limit: <1.3 free space; <0.9 surface (habitats used >60 days, V1 4033)
parameters.caution: Dose rate rising (with space-weather alert → solar storm pattern)
parameters.actions: Check space-weather feed; prepare shelter; review EVA plans.

parameters.name: Solar particle event (proton flux, NOAA S-scale)
parameters.space_reference: S1 = 10 pfu (≥10 MeV), tenfold steps to S5
parameters.warning: Projected event dose ≥200 mSv (80% of 250); nausea or vomiting after a storm
parameters.actions: 1) End any spacewalk within 2 h. 2) Move to the storm shelter. 3) Add shielding from water and stowage. 4) Log each personal dose; record onset time of any nausea. 5) Repeat blood counts if symptoms.
parameters.recipients: Ground dose assessment; report queued if link delayed

parameters.name: Blood-forming organ dose
parameters.actions: Shelter; minimise further exposure; blood counts.

parameters.name: Acute radiation sickness symptoms
parameters.space_reference: Needs >≈0.7 Gy (mild from 0.3 Gy); nausea, vomiting, loss of appetite 1 h–2 days after
parameters.warning: Nausea or vomiting after a storm
parameters.actions: Record onset time; repeat white/lymphocyte counts every 2–3 h for 8–12 h; anti-nausea per checklist.

parameters.name: Cabin CO2 partial pressure
parameters.space_reference: ISS has ranged 1–9; headaches reported ≈2.8–4.5; cough, poor sleep, blurred vision ≈3.5; fatigue, nausea >4.5
parameters.actions: Read CO2 where crew have been working (fixed sensors miss pockets); move to moving air; restore airflow; check scrubber.
parameters.recipients: Ground reviews scrubber performance and backup CO2 removal

parameters.name: Inspired O2 partial pressure
parameters.space_reference: Target 145–155
parameters.actions: Check O2 supply and leaks; check crew SpO2; oxygen masks if low.

parameters.name: Total cabin pressure
parameters.space_reference: 34.5–103 kPa allowed indefinitely
parameters.upper_limit: 103; changes >1 psi no faster than 13.5 psi/min
parameters.actions: Follow depressurisation checklist; masks or suits; isolate leak; reset SpO2 baselines after any atmosphere change.

parameters.name: Cabin temperature
parameters.space_reference: 18–27 for health; 20–25 for performance
parameters.actions: Adjust thermal control; check sleep-station temperature.

parameters.name: Relative humidity
parameters.space_reference: Average >25%; 30–60% supports performance; after landing up to 75% indefinitely
parameters.actions: Adjust humidity control; skin and eye care if dry.

parameters.name: Noise (work 16 h / sleep 8 h)
parameters.space_reference: Work areas NC-50, sleep NC-40; hazardous level 85 dBA; impulse <140 dB peak
parameters.upper_limit: Work 72 dBA (16 h); sleep 50 dBA; hazard 85 dBA
parameters.advisory: Work >60 dBA (protection recommended) or sleep >50 dBA
parameters.actions: Wear hearing protection; find and damp the source; move sleep station if possible.
parameters.basis: ISS noise flight rule; tiers ours
parameters.source: ISS acoustics flight rule B13-152; NASA acoustics brief

parameters.name: Cabin dust (surface only)
parameters.space_reference: Total <3, respirable <1 mg/m³ (general); lunar 0.3, Martian 0.1 mg/m³
parameters.actions: Clean airlock and suits; run filtration; masks; check crew eye/airway symptoms.
parameters.source: NASA lunar dust brief; Mars dust limits (2026)

parameters.name: Combustion products (CO, HCN, HCl, HF)
parameters.space_reference: Monitor ranges: CO 5–1,000 ppm; HCN, HCl, HF 2–50 ppm. Exposure limits are in NASA SMAC tables (not reviewed)
parameters.actions: Fire/toxic-release checklist: masks, isolate module, check SpCO/SpMet in crew.

parameters.name: Drinking water available
parameters.space_reference: ≥2.5 L/person/day + 240 mL per EVA hour
parameters.actions: Ration plan; check recovery system.

patterns.condition: (headache ≥1 OR sleep <6 h) AND 7-day CO2 ≥2.5 mmHg
patterns.tier: Habitat advisory before any personal alert
patterns.action: Show the cabin card first; check CO2 at the crew member's location

patterns.condition: Same symptom logged by ≥2 crew within 24 h
patterns.action: Check air, water and food before individuals

patterns.condition: Sleep <6 h three nights AND reaction test slower than own baseline
patterns.action: Lighter task list plus a wind-down task

patterns.condition: (fluid <2 L/day OR urine <2.5 L/day) AND (dark urine OR high urinary calcium)
patterns.action: Hydration mission; flank pain opens the kidney-scan guide

patterns.condition: (new blur OR Amsler distortion) AND mission day >30
patterns.action: Eye exam task; note for flight surgeon

patterns.condition: (SpCO OR SpMet above own baseline) AND cabin event in last 24 h
(joint pain OR tingling OR skin change) within 24 h of a spacewalk
patterns.tier: Warning; numbness, weakness, confusion or breathing trouble → Emergency

patterns.condition: Dose rate rising AND space-weather alert ≥S1
patterns.tier: Caution; projected event dose ≥200 mSv → Warning
patterns.action: Shelter prompt; show projected dose against 250 mSv

patterns.condition: Exercise below plan 7 days AND fitness <80% of pre-mission

tiers.condition: NEWS2 total 1–4; a value outside personal baseline; shortfall in sleep, exercise, food or fluid; 7-day CO2 at 2.5 mmHg; cumulative radiation at 50% of career limit
tiers.response: Self-care prompt; item added to next private medical conference
tiers.appearance: Blue, info icon, slow pulse; task added to flight plan

tiers.condition: One vital in its score-3 band; a NASA limit crossed on a slow measure (fitness, strength, bone markers, eye scan); 1-h CO2 >3 mmHg; solar storm ≥S1; cumulative dose 75% of career limit
tiers.recipients: Crew member + crew medical officer; note to flight surgeon
tiers.response: Medical officer review within the hour; open the matching protocol
tiers.appearance: Amber triangle; report to ground built (sent or queued); game layer steps back

tiers.condition: NEWS2 total 5–6; a caution with symptoms; CO2 >4.5 mmHg or symptoms in ≥2 crew; projected storm dose ≥200 mSv
tiers.response: Exam now; treatment from the checklist; ground consulted as the link allows
tiers.appearance: Orange diamond, fast pulse; delay banner shows earliest reply time

tiers.condition: NEWS2 total ≥7; collapse, chest pain, breathlessness, new confusion or neurological signs; cabin O2 <122 mmHg; rapid pressure loss; Type II decompression sickness
tiers.recipients: Whole crew and ground at once
tiers.response: Emergency checklist; first aid does not wait for a reply from Earth
tiers.appearance: Red octagon, full-screen banner; data package sent automatically
